localMemoryScan.note: Local fallback scan only; indexed Firestore should not scan 100,000 documents.

bottlenecks.finding: Memory fallback examines up to 1,00,000 leads for scoped sorting/search, producing a 12,500x examined-to-returned ratio for an 8-row dashboard page.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Never use memory fallback for production capacity. Require Firestore indexes and fail readiness checks when the backend reports memory-fallback.

bottlenecks.finding: Dashboard assembly performs metrics, recent-lead, projection, and notification work concurrently. Tail latency follows the slowest dependency.
bottlenecks.recommendation: Keep projection hit rate above 95%, cache metrics, and monitor per-dependency p95 rather than only the aggregate endpoint.

bottlenecks.finding: 500 connected clients received 50000 synchronous in-process deliveries during the benchmark.
bottlenecks.recommendation: For multi-instance production, require Redis pub/sub, cap per-instance connections, and load-test proxy buffering and reconnect storms in staging.

limitations: Managed Firestore network, index, quota, and billing behavior were not measured.
Render/Vercel autoscaling, TLS, proxy buffering, and internet latency were not measured.
Loopback HTTP results are application baselines, not deploy-environment capacity claims.
A staging k6 enterprise run is still required before broad production launch.
